purpose: Fixed report fields for independent simulated beginner participant 3; reports visible UI outcomes only.
persona: Independent simulated beginner, first introduction to RILL, interested in a short melodic instrumental.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: Visible hints, drawing by dragging, direct duplication, an on-screen naming keyboard and direct exports enabled completion. Exact trimming needed several attempts and a Snap change.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: The dark layout, teal waveforms and readable MIDI rectangles looked cohesive and polished; the native white file dialogs were visually separate.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Editing and duplication responded promptly, and WAV export showed elapsed progress then completion. A save dialog briefly drew black and playback reported a dropout. This is a subjective lab-session rating.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Most selected tools explained the mouse gesture. Precise endpoint trimming and a tiny drag without visible effect needed recovery. The dropout message reduced playback confidence.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: All requested task functions were visible and usable: audio, drawn MIDI, an assigned VST3, mouse-only title, project save, WAV and MIDI exports. Only one simple instrument and a short two-track arrangement were tested.

findings.observation: The blank-area 'Double-click for MIDI' hint led directly to the instrument library; Assign instrument created a MIDI clip with Rill Lab Sine shown on its track.

Pencil said 'Draw notes - Drag to set length'; note labels and lengths appeared while drawing, and adding notes beyond the original clip end extended it to four bars. A visible C-sharp note was corrected by dragging it down with Select.
Duplicate displayed 'Click a clip to duplicate'; clicking successive audio and MIDI copies quickly built a 34.286-second arrangement.
Dragging the last clip edges toward the 30-second grid initially produced 30.268 seconds, then 30.134. A four-pixel MIDI edge drag produced no visible shortening.
Selecting Snap 1 bar and dragging the MIDI edge again aligned both track endings and the header showed 0:30.000.

Playback showed a moved playhead at 003.04.89 and active meters on both tracks, but the UI also reported 'Audio output dropout - 1 - Try a larger buffer in Audio setup.' Stopping returned to the beginning. No audible output was verified.

File > Rename project exposed an on-screen keyboard with Clear and Caps controls. Mouse clicks entered Moonlit, and File > Save offered Moonlit.rill in session-3; accepting it removed the unsaved marker.
The native WAV save dialog was briefly a black rectangle before the filename and folder controls appeared on the next observation.

WAV export displayed the 30-second arrangement, format details and an effect-tail checkbox. After disabling tails and accepting Moonlit.wav, elapsed progress changed to an Exported notice. MIDI export similarly accepted Moonlit.mid and showed an Exported notice.

outcome.status: Completed through the UI: a named 30.000-second audio-plus-VST-MIDI arrangement was saved, and both WAV and MIDI Exported notices were observed. File contents remain independently unverified.
outcome.composition: Two tracks at 112 BPM: existing Circuit rhythm audio repeated across the arrangement and a hand-drawn four-bar melodic phrase repeated on an instrument track. Three complete four-bar copies plus a final two-bar trimmed copy span 14 bars. Melody rises from C4 through E4, G4, D4, F4, A4, B4 and C5 before returning lower in the complete phrase.
outcome.playback_observed: Play changed to Pause; a subsequent screenshot showed transport 003.04.89, a moved yellow playhead and lit meters on both tracks. An Audio output dropout count of 1 was also displayed. Playback was stopped before export and left stopped.

limitations: No composition file contents or heard audio were verified; independent coordinator verification follows.
Output paths were established from native save-dialog breadcrumbs and names, not filesystem inspection.
The laboratory uses software graphics and a timer-paced virtual audio sink with 60 ms buffering; the dropout observation is not a physical-device latency or audible-quality result.
Only Rill Lab Sine was used; no claim is made about other third-party plug-ins or broad production feature completeness.
Elapsed time includes screenshot, tool and reporting overhead, so it is not a performance benchmark.
